steps.title: A day and its lengths

options.label: You wake up and eat breakfast. Which part of the day is this?
Which takes longer: a blink or a night of sleep?
Both pencil ends start at the same line. Which pencil is shorter?

steps.hint: Think about the beginning of your usual school day.
steps.explanation: Use time-of-day words and compare lengths from the same start.
steps.shortExplanation: Make, count or compare the objects. Explain what changed.

mathWorkshop.title: A day and its lengths
mathWorkshop.goal: Use time-of-day words and compare lengths from the same start.

tasks.prompt: You wake up and eat breakfast. Which part of the day is this?
tasks.feedback: Breakfast after waking up is usually in the morning.
tasks.hint: Think about the beginning of your usual school day.

tasks.prompt: Which takes longer: a blink or a night of sleep?
tasks.feedback: A blink is very short. A night of sleep lasts much longer.
tasks.hint: Think about whether each activity ends quickly or lasts for hours.

tasks.prompt: Both pencil ends start at the same line. Which pencil is shorter?
tasks.feedback: Pencil A ends first when both start together, so A is shorter.
tasks.hint: Compare the far ends after checking that the starting ends line up.

parentReview.en: Guided practice is ungraded. Completion records the child doing the activities, not a book-question score.

steps.title: Breakfast time
steps.prompt: When do you usually eat breakfast?
steps.hint: Think about what you do soon after waking up.
steps.explanation: We usually eat breakfast in the morning.
steps.shortExplanation: We usually eat breakfast in the morning.

steps.title: Sleep time
steps.prompt: When do you usually go to sleep?
steps.hint: Is it light or dark when you go to bed?

steps.title: A school day
steps.prompt: Put these parts of a school day in order.
steps.hint: What do you do first when the day starts?
steps.explanation: Wake up first, go to school, then eat dinner later.
steps.shortExplanation: Wake up first, go to school, then eat dinner later.

source.answerKeyText: wake up 1, go to school 2, eat dinner 3

steps.title: Which takes longer
steps.hint: Imagine doing each one. Which lasts all night?
steps.explanation: A night of sleep takes much longer than brushing your teeth.
steps.shortExplanation: A night of sleep takes much longer than brushing your teeth.

steps.title: Which is quicker
steps.hint: Which one is over in a moment?
steps.explanation: A blink takes a very short time.
steps.shortExplanation: A blink takes a very short time.

steps.title: Comparing ribbons
steps.prompt: Compare the ribbons. Choose the longest and shortest.
steps.hint: Check the ribbons start at the same line, then compare the other ends.
steps.explanation: Start at the same line. Ribbon b is longest and c shortest.
steps.shortExplanation: Start at the same line. Ribbon b is longest and c shortest.

steps.title: Fair comparing
steps.prompt: To compare two pencils, put their ends on the same line.
steps.hint: What happens if one pencil starts further along?
steps.explanation: Lining up the ends makes the length comparison fair.
steps.shortExplanation: Lining up the ends makes the length comparison fair.

steps.title: Afternoon time
steps.prompt: It is the afternoon. Which of these do you do in the afternoon?

options.label: play in the park after lunch

steps.hint: Afternoon comes after lunch. Breakfast is in the morning.
steps.explanation: After lunch is the afternoon. We eat breakfast in the morning and sleep at night.
steps.shortExplanation: After lunch is the afternoon. We eat breakfast in the morning and sleep at night.

source.answerKeyText: Any real afternoon activity: coming home, lunch, playing, homework.

steps.title: Moon and stars
steps.prompt: The Moon and stars come out at...
steps.explanation: We see the Moon and stars in the dark night sky.
steps.shortExplanation: We see the Moon and stars in the dark night sky.

steps.title: Dinner time
steps.prompt: We usually have dinner in the...
steps.hint: Is dinner early or late in the day?
steps.explanation: Dinner is the meal we usually eat in the evening.
steps.shortExplanation: Dinner is the meal we usually eat in the evening.

steps.title: The longest thing
steps.hint: Which one could you lie down on?
steps.explanation: A bed is longer than a shoe or a spoon.
steps.shortExplanation: A bed is longer than a shoe or a spoon.

steps.title: Lining up
steps.prompt: To compare lengths fairly, line up the...
steps.explanation: Lining up the ends gives both things the same start.
steps.shortExplanation: Lining up the ends gives both things the same start.

steps.title: Opposite of longer
steps.hint: If one ribbon is longer, the other one is…
steps.explanation: Shorter is the opposite of longer.
steps.shortExplanation: Shorter is the opposite of longer.

stickers.meaning: Having greater length when the ends line up.

homeActivities.text: Line up the ends of three spoons or pencils and order their lengths. Predict which daily activity takes longer, then compare.
homeActivities.textAr: حطّوا أطراف ٣ معالق أو أقلام على نفس الخط، ورتّبوهم من الأطول للأقصر. وتوقعوا أنهي حاجة من حاجات اليوم بتاخد وقت أطول، وبعدين قارنوا.
homeActivities.safety: An adult supervises. Keep small objects away from younger children. An adult handles scissors. Use water at the sink, away from electrical items.
homeActivities.safetyAr: لازم شخص كبير يكون موجود. خلّي الحاجات الصغيرة بعيد عن الأطفال الأصغر، والكبير يمسك المقص. أنشطة المية تكون عند الحوض وبعيد عن الكهرباء.
